messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - high GPU queue growth detected in us-west2-gpu-pool-3. queue_len 5m median went from 120 -> 520 (x4). autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions in last 6m. potential customer impact: increased latency / 429s. thread_ts=3625004321

sam_oncall: I'm oncall. pinging infra + ml. standing up a dedicated channel if needed.

maria_sre: seeing p95 latency jump on /v1/generate from 420ms -> 5.2s over last 10m, error 503s and 429s increasing. dashboards show prefill backlog spiking.

dan_ml: last deploy (deploy-bot) rolled v23.7 at 02:14Z to 10% canary in us-west2. change: default context window increased to 32k for better long-form quality, kv-cache enabled aggressively for prefill warmups. suspect ctx increase + kvcache warmup -> memory pressure and longer service times per request.

deploy-bot: deploy v23.7 -> started 2026-03-15T02:14:22Z, canary targets: us-west2 (10%), rollout paused: false.

leo_infra: racking metrics now. autoscaler logs show repeated allocation failures: "QuotaExceeded: requested 8 GPUs, available 0 (region quota=64, used=64)" — looks like we hit region GPU quota ceiling. also some pools hit per-account pool limit. manual scale will fail until quota freed or we re-route.

sam_oncall: ok, mitigation options: 1) pause/rollback v23.7 to v23.6 in us-west2 canary; 2) route traffic to smaller-ctx variant (v23.7-shortctx) if available; 3) enforce per-customer rate limits temporarily; 4) request emergency quota bump with cloud vendor (slow). what do we want to try first?

dan_ml: recommend pause + rollback canary for immediate relief. v23.6 uses 8k default context and no aggressive kvcache warmup. also we can flip routing to older model for heavy customers.

maria_sre: agree rollback. also turn off automatic prefill KV warmups at runtime for the canary group (if toggle exists) to reduce cold-host amplification.

sam_oncall: executing rollback to v23.6 for us-west2 canary now. deploy-bot, run rollback.
\ndeploy-bot: rollback initiated: v23.7 -> v23.6 (canary subset us-west2). command: `rctl rollback --cluster us-west2 --service text-gen --from v23.7 --to v23.6 --subset canary`

deploy-bot: rollback progress: 12/12 canary instances reverted. health checks passing for reverted instances.

maria_sre: monitoring — queue length dropping from 520 -> 210 in 8m, p95 latency falling to 1.1s. error rate still elevated but trending down.

leo_infra: tried manual scale while rollback in progress: `rctl pool scale --pool us-west2-gpu-pool-3 --add 4` returned `ERROR QuotaExceeded`. vendor portal shows us-west2 GPU quota at soft limit, pending requests from other teams. submitted emergency request (ticket #EMG-3419) to vendor. ETA unknown.

sam_oncall: made temporary routing change to divert non-enterprise traffic to europe pool where spare capacity exists. `routing:update --from us-west2 --to eu-west1 --filter non-enterprise` — applied.

tess_cs: FYI CS reports a couple customers pinging with timeouts ~02:20Z. most low-volume customers; 1 enterprise (AcmeCorp) reported visible errors in session-based chat. I've opened support tickets and notified account teams.

anne_prod: estimate of impacted surface: ~12 customers saw elevated errors, skewed to long-context generation calls (prefill heavy). throughput shrink ~8% during spike window. need to prepare postmortem and customer comms.

maria_sre: quick mitigation checklist executed: rollback canary ✅, divert non-enterprise traffic ✅, reduce per-route concurrency limit for open endpoints to 6 -> throttles reduce overload ✅, disable aggressive kvcache warmup on canary hosts (if any) ✅. still waiting on autoscaler health: autoscaler locked due to quota.

dan_ml: follow-up: we should make v23.7 default context opt-in (feature gate) rather than default for rollout. also add kvcache warmup backoff based on host memory pressure. filing PR for gated rollout.

leo_infra: manual remediation attempt to free GPUs: found 2 stale long-running debug jobs in us-west2 (debug-gpu-session-77, debug-gpu-session-81). terminated them to free 4 GPUs. after termination, region free GPUs increased to 4. attempted scale again -> partial success: autoscaler added 2 GPUs but still below needed. `autoscaler:event` shows scale_succeeded: +2, scale_failed: attempted +3 earlier.

sam_oncall: good progress. Maria - keep watching queues for 30m. Dan - hold v23.7 rollout until PR merged and validated. Leo - continue vendor ticket and see if we can borrow capacity from partner pool.

deploy-bot: canary rollback completed at 02:48Z. service health stabilized. full rollback not performed cluster-wide.

maria_sre: current status: queue_len 5m median 210 (baseline ~120), p95 930ms, error rate 429/503 ~0.7% (down from peak 4.1%). no new customer escalations in last 12m.

anne_prod: action items for post-incident: - formal postmortem, - gating for context-length config, - automated kvcache backoff, - autoscaler should surface quota exhaustion alert earlier and fail open to routing policy.

tess_cs: copying impacted customer IDs to support tickets: C-3231, C-5577, C-8890. prepping comms draft to impacted customers.

sam_oncall: handing off to next oncall in 30m. summary for handoff: cause: v23.7 canary increased default context to 32k + aggressive kvcache warmup -> longer per-request GPU time + memory pressure -> queue growth. exacerbated by region GPU quota exhaustion -> autoscaler failed to add enough capacity. mitigations performed: canary rollback, divert non-enterprise traffic to eu-west1, terminate stale debug jobs to free GPUs, reduce per-route concurrency limits, open vendor emergency quota ticket. current impact: reduced to background (0.7% error), ~12 customers saw errors earlier.

kale_next_oncall: taking handoff at 03:12Z. I'll continue monitoring for 2h and follow up on vendor quota ticket. please paste any outstanding runbooks or access notes here.

sam_oncall: thanks all. runbook refs: runbook/gpu-autoscale, runbook/context-rollout, and internal playbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-quotas. I'll leave the incident channel open and tag this thread for postmortem drafting. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident severity moved from P1 -> P2 at 03:10Z after stabilization. incident timeline summary will be exported to ops-archives in 1h.
